summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman, status post orthotopic liver transplant for end-stage liver disease due to hepatitis C, was readmitted from rehabilitation with asymptomatic hyperkalemia (potassium 7.2) secondary to dehydration. She was treated in the emergency department with insulin, calcium gluconate, and Kayexalate, with potassium normalizing to 3.8 within 24 hours. Tube feedings were adjusted to a more dilute formula and increased rate to improve hydration. Her immunosuppressant was transitioned from tacrolimus to sirolimus due to low levels and persistent tremors. Liver function tests showed improvement, and diabetes was stable without insulin requirement during admission. She remained asymptomatic throughout, with stable vital signs and no complications. She was transferred back to rehabilitation on day two with a plan to continue monitoring tremors, nutrition, and medication adherence.
